finalText:
Same props by value ≠ same props by reference. Common causes:

**1. Parent re-renders, child not memoized.** Default React re-renders whole subtree. Props equality never checked unless `React.memo`.

```jsx
const Child = React.memo(function Child({ items }) { ... })
```

**2. New reference each render.** Even with `memo`, these break shallow compare:

```jsx
<Child style={{ color: 'red' }}      // new object
       items={data.filter(Boolean)}   // new array
       onClick={() => save(id)} />    // new function
```

Fix: `useMemo` for objects/arrays, `useCallback` for handlers.

```jsx
const style = useMemo(() => ({ color: 'red' }), [])
const items = useMemo(() => data.filter(Boolean), [data])
const onClick = useCallback(() => save(id), [id])
```

**3. Context.** Child consuming context re-renders on every context value change, ignores `memo` entirely. Same trap: `value={{ user, setUser }}` = new object each parent render. Memoize the value.

**4. `children` prop.** `<Memoized><span/></Memoized>` — JSX children = new element object each render, so `memo` always fails. Hoist children or pass through parent.

**5. Custom compare wrong.** `React.memo(C, (a, b) => ...)` returns `true` = skip render. Backwards from `shouldComponentUpdate`.

Diagnose fast: React DevTools Profiler, "Record why each component rendered" setting. Tells you which prop changed.

Note: re-render ≠ DOM update. React still diffs; no DOM writes if output same. Only optimize if profiler shows real cost.

Paste component + parent, I pin exact cause.
